findings.detail: The reason for option C says that the guide calls self-reported confidence scores unreliable in general. The guide says only that they are unreliable proxies for actual case complexity (5.2-K3). Elsewhere it endorses field-level confidence scores that are calibrated with labeled validation sets (5.5-S3). The reason overstates the guide. Its second clause, that C still picks a record without requesting an identifier, is accurate.

blind_answer.reason: When a lookup returns multiple matching records, the agent should get an additional identifier rather than pick one by heuristic (5.2-K4, 5.2-S5). In this pipeline, the human review queue is where staff can supply that missing identifier. Option A keeps the flawed heuristic. Option C depends on self-reported confidence, which is unreliable. Option D is just another heuristic and can still pick the wrong account.
